Why does a week have exactly seven days?
Days, months and years come from the sky. Weeks don't.
Long ago, Babylonian sky-watchers tracked the Moon closely.
A lunar month lasts about twenty-nine and a half days.
Split into four phases, each lasts roughly seven days.
They also saw seven bright wanderers move across the sky.
The Sun, the Moon, and five visible planets.
Seven became a special number, and the week spread west.
In 321 AD, Rome made the seven-day week official.
That's why we still have Sunday, Monday, and Saturday.
